chapter_name: The Parliamentary System: Legislature and Executive
learning_objective: 🎯 Unpack the inner workings of the Indian Parliament, learn how exciting laws are made, and understand the teamwork between the Legislature and Executive!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: India's Parliament is like a big team divided into two groups: the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). The President of India is also a very important part of the Parliament!

The main job of the Parliament is to make laws. A proposed law is called a 'Bill'. Members debate and discuss the Bill in both Houses, and once passed and signed by the President, it becomes an official Law.

While the Legislature makes laws, the Executive puts them into action. The Prime Minister and their Council of Ministers form the Executive. They run the country daily and make sure the laws are actually followed.

The Parliament keeps a close watch on the Executive. During 'Question Hour', Members of Parliament (MPs) can ask tough questions to the ministers about their work, ensuring the government is answerable to the people.

fun_activity.title: ⚡ The Family Parliament Session
fun_activity.instructions: Gather your family and propose a new 'Bill' for a fun weekend rule, like 'No screen time on Sunday mornings'. Have a friendly debate discussing the pros and cons, then vote on whether to pass the Bill into a Law!

quick_recap: ⭐ The Indian Parliament consists of the President, the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha.
⭐ The Legislature creates and passes laws, while the Executive implements and enforces them.
⭐ The Parliamentary system ensures that the Executive is always accountable and answerable to the Legislature.
